huro-lst-0252.history: The Berardi family's food business began in 1942, when Eurosia "Mama" Berardi and her son Albert started selling fresh-cut french fries at the Midway at Cedar Point, working from Idaho potatoes and a hand-held potato peeler. The fries became as popular as the park itself and, in the family's telling, were a driving factor in the park's early days; they were sold there until Cedar Point stopped allowing private concessions in 1978. In 1979 Albert and Roseanne Berardi opened Berardi's Restaurant in Huron, focusing on fresh home-cooked food. It has remained family owned ever since and is now in the hands of the fourth generation, with many recipes in the family for more than three decades and nearly everything made from scratch.
huro-lst-0252._history_source: https://berardisrestauranthuron.com/about/ (section 'Berardi's History – How It Started') for 1942, Eurosia/Mama Berardi, Albert, the Midway at Cedar Point, the hand-held peeler, the 1978 end of private concessions, the 1979 Huron opening, 4th generation, and 'made from scratch'. The names 'Albert and Roseanne Berardi' come from the operator's HOME page ('Berardi's Restaurant in Huron was opened in 1979 by Albert and Roseanne Berardi and it is still family owned to this day.') — ⚠️ the /about/ page credits the 1979 opening to Albert alone; both are the operator's own words and they differ on whether Roseanne is named. Every clause above traces to one of those two pages. No local-press, Sandusky Register or Huron Historical Society material was consulted (no search available) — additional history is NOT ESTABLISHED, not absent.
